children: River Exchange, the US-based Bitcoin financial services company, has filed a lawsuit against a Canadian Bitcoin mining firm seeking approximately $6.7 million in unpaid refunds. The dispute stems from the cancellation of a contract between the two parties, with River alleging the miner failed to return funds owed after the deal fell apart.
The identity of the Canadian mining company has not been publicly disclosed, nor have the specific terms of the original contract.

The core of the lawsuit centers on a canceled contract between River Exchange and the unnamed Canadian miner. After the agreement was terminated, River claims it was owed refunds totaling between $6.7 million and $7 million, money that the defendant has allegedly refused to pay.
Court filings confirming the jurisdiction and exact filing date have not surfaced in public records. That could mean the case was filed recently or that the proceedings are under seal.

Cross-border disputes between US financial services firms and Canadian mining operations have become a recurring subplot in the Bitcoin mining industry. Similar legal disputes in this sector typically involve equipment or energy supply disagreements, or the termination of service agreements.

The secrecy around the defendant's identity adds another layer. In a sector where public mining companies regularly disclose material litigation in their quarterly filings, the absence of any corresponding disclosure from a Canadian miner suggests the defendant may be a private company.

title: River Exchange sues Canadian Bitcoin miner for $6.7M over unpaid refunds
